subject: Using R-Apaache in real time analysis

messages.author: 075b97c2dac7f3d8
messages.subject: Using R-Apaache in real time analysis
parts:
Hi All,

Apologies for posting a somewhat more general quesiton than just
RApache to this forum. However, during the developement of my first
RApache app in March (http://www.apistat.com/apps/nonparametric/) I
was extremely happy with the quick and very helpfull responses by Jeff
so I thought maybe someone has a sensible advice for my current
problem: (If this is totally in the wrong spot - my apologies...)

I am currently creating a shopping website that adapts the
presentation of products based on responses of individual consumers to
those presentations. Effectively, the time spend on the page is
predicted in [R] by an lmer model with crossed random effects for
different presentation strategies. By using a unique ID for each
customer - which is the same after reoccuring visits - it is possible
to compute presentation-strategy coefficients for individuals (and the
certainty about this estimate) and use these to select the optimal
presentation-strategy for that individual customer.

Currently I am trying to implement this as a REST API service so I can
implement that same backend on multiple sites. My current approach is
as such:
1. There is an API implemented partly in PHP - the shopping site makes
makes a http request and the userID, the presented strategy, and the
time spent on the page are saved in a MySQL database.
2. If the websites request which presentation to show next for the
current user this http request is send directly through [R] apache ->
the current lmer model is updated by grabbing the newest data fram the
MySQL database -> the coefficients are estimated and using a decision
rule based on the estimates for different strategies -> and an id for
the next presentation-strategy to present is replied to the site.

All of this works... However, I am very fearfull that it will not work
if there are 10.000 people on the site, for each interaction creating
another RApapche call, creating the MySQL connection, updating the
model, and estimating the coefficients.... (Actually, already RMySQL
(an [R] package) complaints about too many simulatanious
connectioons..). Also I feel that in the long run refitting the model
every time is costly - even though the partial pooling does improve
the estimate over individual level models...

Hence I am looking for a more scalable option - however, I really want
to be able to refit or update the models in real time (thus, no
nightly cronjob to estimate the coefficients).

Do you feel that it should be possible to scale an application like
this using RApache? Or would I be better of using Python to run the
models?

Any advice on ways to make this efficient would be great!

messages.author: 075b97c2dac7f3d8
messages.subject: Re: Using R-Apaache in real time analysis
parts:
Hi Jeff,

Thanks for the reply. There is no rush, I am still trying different
options...

Jeroen replied and I might be able to beta test the product by Revo
which might do the trick - however, I have not tried it yet. Other
than that I am trying to 'distribute' the models a bit.... Basically I
am computing a partially pooled (multilevel) model and then estimate
coefficients of the different factors of interest for each individual.
Then, when that individaul is interacting in real time I just (bayes)
update their individual function - hence without any pooling. At night
R goes to work and prepares the new estimates.

I think that will work out but I am still at a testing stage where I
try to distribute the computations and run some simulations to see how
well it performs.

If you have any suggestions that would be great.

Cheers,

Maurits
